Resolve prey to the WoRMS classification (id, exact name, then fuzzy)

Source: R/dv_taxonomy.R
dv_taxonomy_worms.Rd

Matches each unique prey to the World Register of Marine Species and returns its lineage for the declared ranks. Matching proceeds in this order:

  1. id - the AphiaID is already known (prey_id). Its WoRMS record is read: an unaccepted AphiaID is followed to its accepted (valid) one ("id_synonym"), and the prey name stored with it is compared with the name WoRMS gives that AphiaID (name_check: "agrees" or "differs"). If the record cannot be read, the AphiaID is used as given ("id_unchecked");

  2. exact - the prey name matches a WoRMS name exactly;

  3. fuzzy - (if fuzzy = TRUE) WoRMS TAXAMATCH (worrms::wm_records_taxamatch()) proposes the closest name, which can rescue a misspelling;

  4. unresolved - nothing matched; all ranks stay NA.

Unaccepted names are followed to their accepted (valid) AphiaID before the lineage is fetched. Every prey carries a provenance record (match_type, name_check, matched_name, aphia_used, n_candidates, homonym, lineage_ok, retrieved) so doubtful matches can be reviewed and corrected - see dv_taxonomy_report(). Nothing is guessed silently: a fuzzy match is flagged, a name with several accepted WoRMS records is flagged as a possible homonym, and an unresolved prey keeps NA ranks and shows up as the explicit unidentified category downstream.

Usage

dv_taxonomy_worms(
  keys,
  ranks = c("kingdom", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "species"),
  cache_dir = tools::R_user_dir("DietView", "cache"),
  fuzzy = TRUE,
  marine_only = TRUE,
  cache_max_age = 180,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

keys

Data.frame with columns prey_id (AphiaID, may be NA) and prey_name (may be NA); one row per unique prey. Other columns are kept.

ranks

Ranks to keep (default the seven flagship ranks).

cache_dir

Directory for the on-disk cache. NULL disables caching.

fuzzy

If TRUE (default), fall back to WoRMS TAXAMATCH fuzzy name matching when the exact name fails. Set FALSE for exact-only, conservative matching.

marine_only

Restrict WoRMS name matching to marine taxa.

cache_max_age

Maximum age, in days, of a cached lookup before it is fetched again (default 180). Inf trusts the cache forever.

verbose

Print progress.

Value

keys with one column per rank plus aphia_used, match_type ("id", "id_synonym", "id_unchecked", "exact", "fuzzy", "unresolved"), name_check, matched_name, n_candidates (WoRMS records returned for a name), homonym (more than one accepted record for that name), lineage_ok (TRUE/FALSE once a classification was requested, NA otherwise) and retrieved (date the lineage was fetched from WoRMS).

Details

Requires the worrms package and internet access. Successful lookups are cached to disk, so re-runs and other surveys do not requery. Failed lookups (timeout, no network, server error, an AphiaID WoRMS does not know) are never cached: they are flagged with lineage_ok = FALSE and a warning, and are retried on the next run. Cache entries written by DietView 0.1.0, which carry no date, are fetched again; the empty lineages it cached after failed lookups are discarded. The cache file is written even if the run is interrupted.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# needs the 'worrms' package and internet access
keys <- data.frame(
  prey_id   = c(126436, NA),
  prey_name = c("Gadus morhua", "Crangon crangon"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
dv_taxonomy_worms(keys)

# the prey keys of the ICES cod records
cod <- ices_diet[ices_diet$predator_common == "Atlantic cod", ]
keys <- unique(data.frame(prey_id = cod$prey_aphia_id,
                          prey_name = cod$prey_name))
lin <- dv_taxonomy_worms(keys)
table(lin$match_type)
} # }
